cim: Mesterséges intelligencia azonosítja a Parkinson-kórt a hang alapján
lead: Egy új kutatás szerint a hangképzési sajátosságok elemzésével a mesterséges intelligencia képes felismerni és megkülönböztetni a Parkinson-kórt.
osszefoglalo:
A [NatureScientific Reportsban](https://www.nature.com/srep) megjelent tanulmányban a kutatók egy **hangalapú digitális biomarkert** fejlesztettek ki, amely nagyjából 1600 résztvevő hangmintái alapján azonosítja a neurodegeneratív betegségeket. A rendszer a hangképzés stabilitását, az artikulációt és a hangminőséget elemzi egy háromlépcsős diagnosztikai folyamat során.

A modell az első szakaszban **0,892-es AUC-értékkel** tudta elkülöníteni az egészséges résztvevőket a betegektől. A második és harmadik lépésben a rendszer a Parkinson-kór különböző alcsoportjait és a hasonló tünetekkel járó esszenciális remegést igyekezett megkülönböztetni egymástól, ahol a teljes folyamat végpontok közötti pontossága 0,533 lett.

Bár a teljes folyamat együttes pontossága még korlátozott, a kísérlet bebizonyította, hogy a hangalapú mesterséges intelligencia hatékony kiegészítő eszközzé válhat a korai szűrésekben és a diagnosztikában.
miert_szamit: Az eredmény jól mutatja, hogy az AI-alapú hang- és beszédelemzés **nem invazív, olcsó szűrőeszközzé válhat** az egészségügyi és diagnosztikai alkalmazásokban.

cim_eredeti: Artificial Intelligence-based hierarchical classification of parkinsonism using digital voice biomarkers
szoveg_eredeti:
Parkinsonian disorders and related movement disorders, including Parkinson disease, essential tremor, multiple system atrophy, and progressive supranuclear palsy, are heterogeneous conditions that can be difficult to differentiate clinically. We developed and validated a voice-based digital biomarker approach using a large-scale dataset of approximately 1600 participants across five diagnostic groups. Acoustic features capturing phonation stability, articulation, and voice quality were extracted, and a hierarchical classification framework reflecting clinical diagnostic workflows was applied. The pipeline consisted of three stages: normal controls versus disease, essential tremor versus Parkinsonism, and differentiation among Parkinsonian subtypes. On an independent test set, the model achieved AUCs of 0.892 and 0.737 in Stages 1 and 2, respectively, and a macro-average one-vs-rest AUC of 0.710 in Stage 3. When evaluated end-to-end, the complete hierarchical pipeline achieved an overall accuracy of 0.533 and an F1-score of 0.404. Explainability analysis identified phonation and articulation features as key contributors to classification. These findings suggest the feasibility of using voice-based digital biomarkers as supportive tools for screening and classification of Parkinsonian disorders.

Parkinson’s disease (PD) is one of the fastest-growing neurodegenerative disorders worldwide, with the number of affected patients increasing substantially over the past few decades. According to recent epidemiological studies, the number of individuals affected by PD has increased from approximately 3.15 million in 1990 to 11.77 million in 2021, representing a nearly 3.7-fold increase. Furthermore, PD shows a strong age dependency, with the highest prevalence observed in individuals aged 80–84 years1. Parkinsonism encompasses a group of neurodegenerative conditions, including PD, multiple system atrophy (MSA), and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), which are characterized by progressive motor impairment and a wide range of neurological symptoms that significantly affect patients’ quality of life2,3. Although essential tremor (ET) is not classified as a Parkinsonian disorder, it shares overlapping clinical features, particularly tremor, making it an important condition in the differential diagnosis of PD4. These disorders often present with similar clinical manifestations, especially in the early stages, making accurate differential diagnosis challenging and limiting early detection5.

Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have facilitated the development of data-driven approaches across diverse biomedical applications, ranging from molecular-level prediction to disease classification and clinical decision support6,7. In PD, numerous studies have explored speech and voice data as digital biomarkers for disease detection and classification8. Voice-based analysis offers several advantages, including its noninvasive nature and cost-effectiveness, and has demonstrated potential for early screening, differential diagnosis, and symptom assessment. In particular, machine learning approaches have been widely applied to classify Parkinsonian disorders and predict disease progression using speech-derived features9.

Recent studies have reported promising results using speech biomarkers for various clinical tasks. For example, Subert et al.10 performed binary classification across multiple disease groups (MSA, PD, and healthy controls) using a balanced dataset with 39 patients per class, reporting AUC values of 0.81 for MSA vs. PD, 0.88 for MSA vs HC, and 0.74 for PD vs HC. Sousa et al.11 focused on predicting motor symptoms in PD rather than simple classification, achieving an AUC of 0.86 using speech features, suggesting their potential in reflecting disease severity.
